# Reinforcement and Decay Dynamics {#sec-reinforcement}

## Memory Strength and Eviction (Removed) {#sec-memory-strength}

Earlier builds kept multi-timescale strength traces per memory (fast, medium, slow and ultra-slow, mixed into `strength`). Every retrieval reinforced or decayed them, and memories whose effective strength fell below `PeripheryCutoff(T)` were evicted. Eviction waited for two gates. The first was a consolidation watermark: a memory had to predate `last_consolidation_ts`. The second was a storage floor, by default 500 MB per file-backed store.

The engine ablation study (2026-10) removed the traces, the reinforcement and decay update, eviction, its storage-pressure gate and its `memory_evictions` audit log. At the default knobs eviction never ran. The consolidation watermark was never set, because clustering consolidation never produced a candidate (@sec-consolidation). Phase-1 ablation of the strength update left every packet byte-identical: Eval 1 0/250, LongMemEval-S 0/48, BEAM-10M 0/40. A fix that made consolidation fire also opened the eviction gate. With the storage floor at 0, eviction then deleted 94% of LongMemEval-S memories, 92% of Eval 1 memories and 99.7% of a 22.6k-turn BEAM-10M conversation. Packet gold-turn recall fell from 0.630 to 0.086, from 0.587 to 0.084, and from 0.103 to 0. Turn timestamps span weeks to months, and strength decayed against a half-life of minutes to hours, so almost every memory looked "weak" once the gate opened.

`strength` now holds only its knob-derived initial value, adjusted by retrieval-induced suppression (@sec-advanced). A slim `RecordMemoryUsage` step keeps the retrieval counters that hydrated memories expose: `retrieved_count`, `used_count`, `last_used` and `last_access`. Store growth is unbounded again. A bounded store needs a forgetting policy that is measured against recall first.

## Contextual Gain and Per-Memory Stability (Definitions)

Contextual gain is a per-retrieval signal used by multiple feedback loops:

```
contextual_gain_t(m) ← cos(μ_acc, m.embedding)    # if m was retrieved and used (range [−1, 1])
contextual_gain_t(m) ← undefined                # otherwise
```

When undefined, treat contextual_gain_t(m) as 0 in downstream updates. It is not persisted (the smoothed per-memory column was removed with memory strength).

Per-memory stability initializes at creation and is bounded:

```
strength(m)_init = memory_initial_strength(F,S,T)
stability(m)_init = memory_initial_stability(F,S,T)
stability(m) ← clamp(stability(m), 0.0, 2.0)
```

Retrieved vs used:

```
retrieved(m) = memory returned by vector retrieval
used(m) = retrieved(m) AND injected into active context after gate decisions
```

Contextual gain is only measured for used memories.

## Reinforcement Graph Maintenance

The normal interrupt gate injects at most one selected memory into active
context per dispatch. Production retrieval therefore does not synthesize a
pairwise *reinforces* edge from its broader retrieved packet: packet
co-occurrence is not evidence that two memories were used together. This also
prevents repeated noisy packets from turning boilerplate into durable graph
hubs.

Retrieval no longer traverses association edges, so existing *reinforces*
edges in older stores are inert.

## Causal Feedback Loop {#sec-feedback}

The system tracks causal influence of retrieved memories on generation quality through contextual gain—the semantic alignment (cosine similarity) between the current signal embedding and the retrieved memory embedding.

### Focus Feedback (Removed)

Earlier builds adjusted `weight_relevance` and `attention_width` from the contextual gain of used memories. They also dilated the attention width with drift and pulled it back toward its prior every turn. The engine ablation study (2026-10) removed this step. With it switched off as part of the minor-feedback group, packets stayed byte-identical: Eval 1 0/250, LongMemEval-S 0/48, BEAM-10M 0/40. `weight_relevance` and `attention_width` now stay at their knob-derived priors unless `UpdateFocus` moves them.

### Sensitivity Feedback (Removed)

Earlier builds nudged `weight_novelty` by `η_base × (novelty_reward × contextual_gain − redundancy)` for used memories, and persisted a per-memory `redundancy` that fed only the clustering-consolidation score. The engine ablation study (2026-10) removed the step, the `redundancy` column, and the never-written `connectivity` column. With the step switched off as part of the minor-feedback group, packets stayed byte-identical: Eval 1 0/250, LongMemEval-S 0/48, BEAM-10M 0/40.

### Stability Feedback

```
γT_base = 0.05
for each used memory m:
    if contextual_gain(m) > 0:
        stability_t(m) ← stability(m) + γT_base
    else:
        stability_t(m) ← stability(m) × (1 − γT_base)
    stability(m) ← clamp(stability_t(m), 0.0, 2.0)
```

The mean stability of used memories provides adjustment to the half-life target:

```
adj ← clamp(mean(stability(m_used)) − 1.0, −0.25, +0.25)
ΔHalfLife_adj_t ← adj
```

This factor is consumed by the Stability update (@sec-stability-update), avoiding conflicting adjustments between feedback mechanisms.

## Influence Feedback (Removed)

Earlier builds ran an influence-feedback operation (Algorithm 19). It blended contextual gain with neutral generation-similarity and drift terms into per-memory `influence`, `sustained_influence` and `mean_influence` columns. Nothing downstream read those columns. The engine ablation study (2026-10) removed the operation and its columns. With it switched off as part of the minor-feedback group, packets stayed byte-identical: Eval 1 0/250, LongMemEval-S 0/48, BEAM-10M 0/40.
